title: Prove sharp forward macro-prefix bound for parity recursion
body:
The forward-only 3/2 question left open by #4731 now has an all-size proof: every forward macro-prefix of the exact triangular parity recursion has infinity norm at most `1+η` when `0≤η≤1`, for every dyadic dimension and every legal interleaving of its disjoint children. The bound is sharp at a proper four-wire prefix.

The proof sets `R=P T^(-1)` and shows that `P−I` and `R−I` have disjoint supports. The row identity `H−G=(I+G)(T−I)` then gives `h_i+(1−η)g_i≤η`. This resolves the half-tail forward-only question and extends the lemma through η=1. It does not change #4731's common four-cut bound, the selected frontier, or the separate internal-gate/rounding/Gaussian accounting obligations.

Canonical claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4715#discussioncomment-19130279

The package includes exact source pins, a quantified proof, family coverage and open next questions. A DAG-cut checker reuses retained pure matrix helpers and compares matrices reached through different legal interleavings. It checks seven rational fixtures of sizes 1,2,4,8 (all 123 eight-wire cuts), sharp proper prefixes, η=1 inverse-growth controls, and five negative controls including an exact η=2 counterexample to extending the claimed bound indiscriminately.
